analysis:
The only change in this PR is documentation in docs/developer/test.md. It adds a new 'Prompt Preparation And Admission' section at head lines 323-341. The section documents a swift test selector (PromptTokenCacheTests, ChatTemplateLoopRewritesTests, InboundChatRequestDecodeTests, ServeLoopColdLoadTests), the PROMPT_TOKEN_CACHE_MODEL_DIRS environment variable, and the `darkbloom benchmark --prompt-prep --model <id>` command. No source, configuration, workflow, key-handling or protocol code is changed.

I checked the added text against the threat model assets and boundaries (A-001 prompts, TB-002, TB-007, T-041 prefix cache). The section does not instruct anyone to relax a control, disable encryption, or use production state. It describes tests using synthetic tokenizers with no download. The optional real-model-dir variable reads only local model directories that the operator supplies.

A possible concern is that the benchmark and tests touch prompt content. The documented benchmark runs only on CPU with a tokenizer loaded and does not use real consumer traffic. The text does not say telemetry or logs receive prompts. No unverified contract materially affects a security conclusion. The underlying code for prompt token caching (PromptTokenCache) and the merged admission body decode is not in this batch. Any later review of those code changes should check that cached token IDs are not shared across tenants. That would touch T-041 and its cacheSalt scoping, as well as the plaintext-in-memory handling for A-001. Because this PR only describes tests, I report no findings.
